answer.answer: Scrapy makes Twisted's AsyncioSelectorReactor the default TWISTED_REACTOR so that asyncio and asyncio-based libraries work in any coroutine, and new projects need no extra setup (decision 'asyncio reactor by default', status accepted, from docs/topics/asyncio.rst). The default is set in scrapy/settings/default_settings.py (module scrapy.settings.default_settings), line 609: TWISTED_REACTOR = "twisted.internet.asyncioreactor.AsyncioSelectorReactor". If you use CrawlerRunner or AsyncCrawlerRunner, you still have to install the reactor yourself with scrapy.utils.reactor.install_reactor.

Scrapy defaults TWISTED_REACTOR to 'twisted.internet.asyncioreactor.AsyncioSelectorReactor' because that reactor turns on native asyncio support. With it you can use asyncio and asyncio-based libraries in any coroutine, and new projects made with startproject need no extra setup (docs/topics/asyncio.rst:7-27; decision:asyncio-reactor-default). The default is set in scrapy/settings/default_settings.py at line 609, which is the module scrapy.settings.default_settings. Line 608 there also sets TWISTED_REACTOR_ENABLED = True. If you use CrawlerRunner or AsyncCrawlerRunner, you still have to install the reactor yourself with scrapy.utils.reactor.install_reactor (docs/topics/asyncio.rst:29-38).

docs/topics/settings.rst documents DOWNLOAD_DELAY as 'Default: 1 (fallback: 0)'. The same doc explains that when startproject sets a value in the settings.py it generates, that value is documented as the default, and the value from scrapy.settings.default_settings is documented as the fallback. So the fallback 0 is set in scrapy/settings/default_settings.py (line 292, DOWNLOAD_DELAY = 0). The default 1 comes from the startproject settings template, scrapy/templates/project/module/settings.py.tmpl, which startproject renders into <project>/settings.py (TEMPLATES_TO_RENDER, with templates_dir = scrapy/templates/project). The graph has no node for that template, so I could not read the file to see the line that sets 1.

docs/topics/settings.rst documents DOWNLOAD_DELAY's default as 1, with a fallback of 0. The value 1 comes from the project template scrapy/templates/project/module/settings.py.tmpl (DOWNLOAD_DELAY = 1), which ends up in the settings.py of projects generated with startproject. The fallback 0 comes from scrapy/settings/default_settings.py (DOWNLOAD_DELAY = 0).

The file docs/topics/item-pipeline.rst ("Item Pipeline", section "Writing your own item pipeline") explains how to write an item pipeline component. It says each component must implement process_item(self, item), which returns an item or raises DropItem, and may also implement open_spider(self), called when the spider opens and allowed to raise CloseSpider, and close_spider(self), called when the spider closes, before the spider_closed signal. Any of these may be coroutine functions (async def).

The default request fingerprinter is the class RequestFingerprinter, defined in the module scrapy.utils.request (scrapy/utils/request.py, lines 118-138). Its docstring reads 'Default fingerprinter.' By default Scrapy computes request fingerprints with the RequestFingerprinter class, set by the REQUEST_FINGERPRINTER_CLASS default setting to "scrapy.utils.request.RequestFingerprinter" and loaded by the crawler. The class is defined in the scrapy.utils.request module.

The retry downloader middleware is RetryMiddleware, defined in the module scrapy.downloadermiddlewares.retry (scrapy/downloadermiddlewares/retry.py). Its __init__ raises NotConfigured unless the RETRY_ENABLED setting is true, so RETRY_ENABLED turns it on. RETRY_TIMES sets the maximum number of retries (self.max_retry_times), and a request's max_retry_times meta key can override it per request.

The retry downloader middleware is RetryMiddleware in the module scrapy.downloadermiddlewares.retry. It is turned on by the RETRY_ENABLED setting (default True; if false, the middleware raises NotConfigured), and RETRY_TIMES sets how many times a request is retried (default 2, i.e. the initial request plus 2 retries).

Scrapy's default settings do not define a requests-per-second rate, so the sources give no fixed number. The defaults cap concurrency, not throughput: CONCURRENT_REQUESTS = 16 overall and CONCURRENT_REQUESTS_PER_DOMAIN = 8. DOWNLOAD_DELAY = 0, so there is no delay between requests, and AUTOTHROTTLE_ENABLED = False. The real rate therefore depends on server latency and network conditions (roughly concurrency divided by response time), and is not set by any setting. The settings documentation does not state a per-second figure either.

The defaults cap concurrency, not rate: CONCURRENT_REQUESTS = 16 overall and CONCURRENT_REQUESTS_PER_DOMAIN = 8, with DOWNLOAD_DELAY = 0 and AUTOTHROTTLE_ENABLED = False. So no delay or throttle limits throughput, and the real rate depends on server latency and response times. Note that the project template generated by startproject does set DOWNLOAD_DELAY = 1, about 1 request per second per domain, but that is the template, not the default.

The repository does not establish whether scrapy.core.scheduler.Scheduler is thread-safe. Its docstring and the scheduler docs (docs/topics/scheduler.rst) describe priority queues, request order, JOBDIR persistence and dupefilters, but say nothing about threads, locks or thread safety, and the class source has no threading or locking primitives. The only related statement is architectural: Scrapy is built on Twisted and uses non-blocking asynchronous code for concurrency rather than threads (docs/topics/architecture.rst:151-156), which implies the scheduler is driven from a single event loop. That does not amount to a thread-safety guarantee, and no test covers concurrent access either.

The repository does not establish whether scrapy.core.scheduler.Scheduler is thread-safe. scrapy/core/scheduler.py contains no mention of threads, locks or thread safety; its only concurrency discussion (the 'Concurrency affects order' section of the Scheduler docstring) concerns concurrent requests (CONCURRENT_REQUESTS / CONCURRENT_REQUESTS_PER_DOMAIN) affecting crawl order, not thread safety. A repo-wide search for 'thread-safe' only finds asyncio call_soon_threadsafe / run_coroutine_threadsafe usages in crawler.py, shell.py and docs/topics/asyncio.rst, none about the scheduler. So the repository neither claims nor denies that Scheduler is thread-safe.
